info: The show list is the show_* folders of the selected channel. The same show name may exist on another display.
New shows are not activated automatically.
Auto-optimize uses the bulk of dark and light pixels, not short histogram spikes.
Disabled controls show a not-allowed cursor.
Auto-optimize uses the subject (or the image center) so night photos and bright high-key shots keep faces visible.
Adding photos disables Back and warns before the tab is closed.
Activate Show is back in the main menu.
Installer runtimes: Apache Lounge zip pin updated; PHP Windows builds moved to 8.4.27-1 after 8.4.26 disappeared.
Installer runtime download resumes and retries after a truncated Node.js zip (curl error 18).
Firmware compiles again: rest-period time math no longer uses a name that PNGdec defines as a macro.
COCO-SSD model.json pin matches the current TensorFlow.js download.
Per-show rest period (default 22:00–06:00). The frame keeps the last photo and stays in deep sleep; the same start and end hour turns rest off.
Server packages download the local COCO-SSD model from the committed manifest so the release build can run without vendored weights.
Web UI and firmware config use i18x for en-US, de-DE and zh-CN. Language defaults to the browser and can be changed in the header or the frame AP.
The firmware stores Server URL and User ID when groups are loaded, so the config form keeps them after a page reload.
Config and status text refresh the full native panel. Spectra 6 no longer leaves color noise on the right from a rotated partial update.
Waveshare 1.54G enables deep sleep by default (own charge circuit). NeoFrame stays off so USB power banks do not cut out.
One display-ID table everywhere (docs/technical_overview.md). Spectra 6 7.3" is 9 (E1002 / NeoFrame); I is BWR 2.13" again. No aliases or path remapping.
A channel is User ID / Group ID / display. The firmware AP takes Server URL and User ID; the server lists Group IDs for that display.
ink-encoder 2.1.0 on npm uses the same catalog. Existing shows must be recreated from original photos.
Firmware upload from µGulp finds PlatformIO in the user install, streams pio logs, and uses a connected USB serial port instead of a hardcoded COM number.
Upload stops with a clear error if no data USB device is present. The USB chip (CH340 vs native CDC) is only a hint — choose Target explicitly.
Firmware builds again: status helpers no longer repeat default arguments.
Waveshare ESP32-S3 1.54inch e-Paper (G) is a first-class firmware target: 200×200 BWRY, display ID f, official wiki pin map, native USB-C, no battery.
If the photo server is offline, the last successfully loaded image stays on the panel instead of a loading or error screen.
Status and config text follow the frame orientation; .ink pixels stay in native panel layout.
Buttonless boards keep deep sleep off by default so USB power banks do not cut off.
NeoFrame (GooDisplay GDP073EW1 / GDEP073E01) is a first-class firmware target with the same Spectra 6 display ID I as the reTerminal E1002.
NeoFrame uses the official ESP32E6-E01 pin map, 8 MB PSRAM for 800×480 decode, and a 5-minute open config AP after power-on (no buttons).
Random slideshow plays every image once per cycle; very large shows fall back safely.
Factory restore for the vendor NeoFrame image.
Optionally store only one aspect ratio.
Automatic per-photo optimization for the target display.
Firmware: deep sleep on by default, unpaired .ink files used in any orientation, version display.
